dimensions.name: network_calls
dimensions.label: New or changed network calls
dimensions.reasoning: cdn.js adds a setInterval that fires every 2000ms and calls fetch() to 'https://verify.titaniumnetwork.org/callback/' with a random path. This is a recurring beacon/ping to an external server. While it uses 'no-cors' mode (limiting response reading), the outbound call itself is a persistent network side-effect introduced unconditionally. sw.js also proxies arbitrary web requests through a ScramjetServiceWorker and calls fetch() on behalf of intercepted requests, broadening the network footprint significantly.

dimensions.name: resource_exhaustion
dimensions.label: Denial-of-service / resource-exhaustion patterns (unbounded loops, recursion, unthrottled blocking calls)
dimensions.reasoning: cdn.js uses setInterval(..., 2000) with no clear termination condition, meaning it will fire indefinitely as long as the environment is active, making repeated network calls. While this is not a tight infinite loop, it does constitute an unbounded periodic resource drain (network connections every 2 seconds forever). This is anomalous for a package named 'ilovefemboys' and constitutes a persistent background load.

llm_summary: Version 2.0.0 of this package adds two new files with highly suspicious behaviour. cdn.js installs a persistent setInterval beacon that fires every 2 seconds to an external server (verify.titaniumnetwork.org) with a random callback path, constituting an unbounded network drain and potential tracking/exfiltration mechanism. sw.js registers a service worker that proxies web traffic through the Scramjet obfuscating proxy library and injects a JavaScript payload into every HTML response, intercepting window.open calls, anchor clicks, and form submissions to redirect or relay tab-opening actions through postMessage — a pattern consistent with adware or traffic-hijacking. The combination of a persistent network beacon, a service-worker-level HTML injector, and click/navigation interception in a package with no obvious legitimate use-case for these features represents a strong supply-chain risk signal.
